mainTopic: What counts as נכסי, and gifts of property: a gift made because of a marriage, and the gift of a שכיב מרע
overview: The גמרא finishes a list of belongings that count as נכסי ("property"). Documents, animals, birds and תפילין are all included, each proven from a ברייתא or a משנה. It then asks whether a ספר תורה counts, since it normally may not be sold but may be sold to learn Torah or to marry. That question ends as תיקו. Next comes a סימן, a memory aid, followed by real cases about gifts of property. A woman who gave her property to her son because she was getting married, and was later divorced, can take it back, because she openly tied the gift to the marriage. Several cases teach the rules of a שכיב מרע, a dying person. Following שמואל, he may take back his gift and give it to someone else. His spoken words alone transfer the gift, with no act of acquisition. The amud ends as a new story begins about רב דימי בר יוסף's sister and her orchard.

steps.title: Deeds count as property
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a deed is acquired together with land, using the rule about נכסים שאין להם אחריות. So documents are called נכסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A scribe may write a deed for the seller even if the buyer isn't there. Once the buyer takes possession of the land, he also acquires the deed, wherever it is. This matches what we learned: property that does not serve as a guarantee is acquired together with property that does (land), through money, a deed, or a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its proof that legal documents count as נכסי. It does this by quoting a ברייתא about writing a deed of sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deed is acquired through the buyer's חזקה on the land, and the ברייתא links this to the rule that נכסים שאין להם אחריות go along with land. That means a document is a kind of נכסים. So when someone gives away "my נכסי," his documents are included.

keyTerms.meaning: took possession through a physical act (חזקה)
movable property that cannot be collected from by a creditor
land, which serves as a guarantee for debts

phrases.english: We may write a deed for the seller

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹקֵחַ עִמּוֹ;
phrases.english: even though the buyer is not with him;
once this one (the buyer) has taken possession of the land,
the deed is acquired, wherever it is.
And this is what we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in קידושין 26a.

phrases.english: Property that does not serve as a guarantee

phrases.aramaic: נִקְנִין עִם הַנְּכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן אַחְרָיוּת –
phrases.english: is acquired together with property that serves as a guarantee
by money, by a deed, or by taking possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוֹתְבִין שְׁטָר לַמּוֹכֵר וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹקֵחַ עִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier list proving which items are called נכסי. This proof is for documents.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about writing a deed, tied to the משנה in קידושין that calls such items נכסים שאין להם אחריות

steps.title: Animals count as property
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about someone who gives all his נכסים to הקדש deals with animals that were part of those נכסים. So animals are called נכסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal is called "property," as the משנה says: if someone consecrates his property and among it are animals fit for the altar, the males become עולות and the females are sold for שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that animals are included in the word נכסי. It points to a משנה that treats animals as part of "his נכסים" given to הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה starts with "one who consecrates his נכסים" and then explains what happens to his animals. That only makes sense if animals are part of his נכסים. What happens to them afterward does not matter for this proof.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not about the rules of קרבנות. It is only that the משנה counts animals as part of "his נכסים."

phrases.english: An animal is called "property,"
as we learned in a משנה:
One who consecrates his property
and among them there was an animal
fit for the altar:
the males are burnt offerings,
and the females are sold
for use as peace offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהֵמָה אִיקְּרִי נִכְסֵי, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the next item to the list of things called נכסי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שקלים about one who consecrates his property

steps.title: Birds count as property
steps.stepSummary: Another משנה about consecrating one's נכסים lists birds among the items fit for the altar. So birds are called נכסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Birds are called "property," as the משנה says: if someone consecrates his property and among it are items fit for the altar, such as wines, oils and birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same kind of proof for birds. A משנה lists birds among the items included in "his נכסים."
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like the proof for animals. Because the משנה names birds as part of the consecrated נכסים, birds fall under the word נכסי.

phrases.english: Birds are called "property,"
as we learned in a משנה:
One who consecrates his property
and among them there were items
that are fit for the altar:
wines, oils, and birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹפוֹת אִיקְּרִי נִכְסֵי, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern of proof as the step about animals, now for birds.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שקלים listing wines, oils and birds among consecrated property

steps.title: תפילין count as property
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that when someone consecrates his נכסים, his תפילין are valued for him. So תפילין are called נכסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: תפילין are called "property," as the משנה says: if someone consecrates his property, his תפילין are valued for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that even a holy object like תפילין counts as נכסי. A משנה treats them as part of what was given to הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תפילין must be valued, which means they were included when he consecrated "his נכסים." So even a מצוה item someone uses personally is part of his property. This sets up the next question about a ספר תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: they assess the value for him

phrases.english: תפילין are called "property,"
as we learned in a משנה:
One who consecrates his property,
his תפילין are assessed for him.
phrases.notes: Their value is set, and he can redeem them by paying that amount to הקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּפִלִּין אִיקְּרִי נִכְסֵי, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the list to a holy object, which leads into the ספר תורה question.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in ערכין about valuing תפילין of one who consecrated his property

steps.title: Does a Torah scroll count as property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a ספר תורה counts as נכסי. There are two sides: it normally may not be sold, but it may be sold to learn Torah or to marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what about a ספר תורה? Since it may not be sold, maybe it is not "property." Or perhaps, since it may be sold in order to learn Torah or to marry a woman, it is "property"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a real question (an איבעיא) about whether a ספר תורה is included in נכסי. It lays out a reason for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test behind the question is whether something you generally cannot sell still counts as your property. Side one: the sale ban means it is not normal property. Side two: since there are allowed sales (to learn Torah or to marry), it is sellable enough to count.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked of them

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
A Torah scroll, what is it?
Since it is not sold,
because it is forbidden to sell it,
it is not "property";
or perhaps,
since it may be sold
in order to study Torah or to marry a woman,
it is "property"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving תפילין are נכסי, the גמרא asks about a holier item that comes with a ban on selling it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a ספר תורה, which generally may not be sold, is included in the word נכסי

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question about the ספר תורה is left as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether a ספר תורה counts as נכסי. Both sides stay possible, so the topic closes with the doubt still open.
steps.whatToRemember: Documents, animals, birds and תפילין are all called נכסי. Whether a ספר תורה is included remains an open question (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 5 without a decision.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a ספר תורה is called נכסי is unresolved.

steps.title: Memory aid for the coming stories
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, a list of key words to help remember the order of the cases that come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: זוטרא, the mother of עמרם, from two sisters, רב טובי, and רב דימי and רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. The גמרא is preparing for a new series of cases by giving a memory aid for their order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the סימן points to one of the upcoming cases. It closes off the list of what counts as נכסי and opens the next section.

phrases.english: (Memory aid:
Zutra, the mother of Amram,
from two sisters,

phrases.aramaic: רַב טוֹבִי וְרַב דִּימִי וְרַב יוֹסֵף.)
phrases.english: Rav Tovi, and Rav Dimi and Rav Yosef.)

steps.triggerLanguage: סִימָן: זוּטְרָא, אִימֵּיהּ דְּעַמְרָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A transition. The list about נכסי is finished, and a memory aid introduces the next cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. It is a memory aid listing key words for the upcoming cases.

steps.title: A mother gives her property to her son before marrying, then is divorced
steps.stepSummary: The mother of רב זוטרא בר טוביא gave her property to her son because she planned to marry רב זביד. She married, was divorced, and came to רב ביבי בר אביי. He ruled that she gave the gift because of the marriage, and the marriage did happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: The mother of רב זוטרא בר טוביא wrote her property over to רב זוטרא בר טוביא, because she wanted to marry רב זביד. She married him, and he divorced her. She came before רב ביבי בר אביי. He said: She gave it because of the marriage, and she did get married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case. A woman gave her property to her son before marrying, and after her divorce she wanted it back. רב ביבי בר אביי ruled that the gift stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman gave the gift for one reason: she was getting married. רב ביבי's logic is that the reason was fulfilled, because she did marry. The later divorce does not change that, so the son keeps the property.

keyTerms.meaning: She wrote over her property (as a gift in a document)

phrases.english: The mother of Rav Zutra bar Toviyya

phrases.aramaic: כַּתְבִינְהוּ לְנִכְסַהּ לְרַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּא,
phrases.english: wrote her property over to Rav Zutra bar Toviyya,
because she wanted to marry Rav Zevid.
She married, and he divorced her.

phrases.aramaic: אָתְיָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי,
phrases.english: She came before Rav Beivai bar Abaye,
He said: It was because of the marriage, and she did get married.
phrases.notes: His point is that what she gave the gift for already happened, so the gift stays with the son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִימֵּיהּ דְּרַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּא כַּתְבִינְהוּ לְנִכְסַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the סימן in step 7, the גמרא begins the first case on the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ביבי בר אביי: a gift given because of a planned marriage stays valid once the marriage happens, even if she is later divorced.

steps.title: רב הונא objects: she made her reason clear, and the marriage ended
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע sharply rejects רב ביבי's ruling. Even the view that a woman's gift made to keep property from her husband is valid applies only when she did not state her reason. Here she made clear it was because of the marriage, and the marriage ended in divorce, so she can take the property back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said to him: Because you come from the 'cut-short' family, you say 'cut-short' things? Even according to the one who says a woman who hides her property from her husband gives a gift that works, that is only when she did not show her reason. But here she showed that it was because of the marriage, and she married and was divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע attacks רב ביבי's ruling. He says the woman should get her property back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually there is a debate about whether a gift made to hide property from a future husband (a מבריחה) really works. רב הונא says that even the view that it works only means a case where she kept her reason hidden. Here she openly tied the gift to the marriage, and now she is no longer married, so the reason for the gift is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who 'hides' her property from her future husband by giving it away
She showed her intention (made her reason clear)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב הונא rejects the view that a מבריחה's gift works. He grants that view (אפילו למאן דאמר), but says it does not cover a case where she openly tied the gift to the marriage.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to him:
Because you come from the 'cut-short' family,
phrases.notes: A sharp play on words: רב ביבי came from the family of עלי the כהן, whose descendants were cursed to die young (שמואל א 2:31).

phrases.english: do you say cut-short things?
Even according to the one who says that a woman who hides her property makes a gift that works,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא גַלְּיָא דַּעְתַּהּ,
phrases.english: that is only where she did not show her intention,
but here, she showed her intention
that it was because of the marriage,
and she married and was divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: מִשּׁוּם דְּאַתּוּ מִמּוּלָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks רב ביבי's ruling from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ביבי בר אביי's ruling that the gift stays with the son after the divorce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She openly tied the gift to the marriage, so it depends on the marriage. Once she is divorced, the reason is gone and the gift goes back to her.
steps.whatToRemember: If a woman openly gives her property away because she is getting married, the gift depends on that marriage. When the marriage ends, she can take the property back.

steps.title: A mother gives her property to one son at night and another son in the morning
steps.stepSummary: The mother of רמי בר חמא gave her property to רמי in the evening and to his brother רב עוקבא the next morning. רב ששת ruled for רמי, and רב נחמן ruled for רב עוקבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The mother of רמי בר חמא wrote her property to רמי בר חמא in the evening. In the morning she wrote it to רב עוקבא בר חמא. רמי בר חמא came before רב ששת, and he put him in charge of the property. רב עוקבא בר חמא went before רב נחמן, and he put him in charge of the property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story with two opposite rulings. Two judges each gave the same property to a different brother. This sets up the argument between them in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת followed the first gift, so the evening gift to רמי wins. רב נחמן followed the later gift to רב עוקבא, which treats the morning gift as taking back the evening gift. The next step explains the reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: He established him in the property (ruled it belongs to him)

phrases.english: The mother of Rami bar Ḥama,

phrases.aramaic: בְּאוּרְתָּא כְּתַבְתִּינְהוּ לְנִכְסַהּ לְרָמִי בַּר חָמָא,
phrases.english: in the evening wrote her property to Rami bar Ḥama;

phrases.aramaic: בְּצַפְרָא כְּתַבְתִּינְהוּ לְרַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא.
phrases.english: in the morning she wrote it to Rav Ukva bar Ḥama.
phrases.notes: רב עוקבא is רמי's brother; she gave the same property twice.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת,
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama came before Rav Sheshet;
he established him in the property.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל רַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: Rav Ukva bar Ḥama went before Rav Naḥman;
he established him in the property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִימֵּיהּ דְּרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא, בְּאוּרְתָּא כְּתַבְתִּינְהוּ לְנִכְסַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case from the סימן list, unrelated to the marriage story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת gave the property to the first receiver (רמי). רב נחמן gave it to the second receiver (רב עוקבא).

steps.title: רב ששת asks: How could she take it back, if she died?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks רב נחמן why he ruled for רב עוקבא. If it is because the mother took back her first gift, she died, so how can that work?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת came before רב נחמן and said to him: What is the reason the Master gave the property to רב עוקבא בר חמא? If it is because she took back her gift, but she died!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת challenges רב נחמן's ruling. He thinks the mother could not cancel her evening gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'but she died' show that the mother was on her deathbed and died from that illness. רב ששת seems to hold that since she never recovered, the first gift to רמי stayed in place, so her morning gift could not cancel it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן, אֲמַר לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet came before Rav Naḥman and said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא אוֹקְמֵיהּ מָר לְרַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא?
phrases.english: What is the reason the Master established Rav Ukva bar Ḥama in the property?
phrases.notes: 'The Master' (מר) is a polite way of saying 'you', meaning רב נחמן.

phrases.english: If it is because she retracted it,
but she died!
phrases.notes: This tells us she was sick and died from it, so we are dealing with a deathbed gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא אוֹקְמֵיהּ מָר לְרַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא? אִי מִשּׁוּם דַּהֲדַרָא בַּהּ – וְהָא שְׁכִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling giving the property to רב עוקבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only reason to prefer the second son is that she took back the first gift. But she died without recovering, so (רב ששת thinks) the first gift stays.

steps.title: רב נחמן answers with שמואל's rule about taking back a gift
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes שמואל: any time the sick person would be able to take back the gift if he recovered, he may also take back his gift while still sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what שמואל said: Whenever, if he got up from his illness, he could take it back, he can take back his gift.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his ruling by quoting a rule from שמואל. This rule allows the mother to cancel her evening gift with her morning gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deathbed gift that gives away everything is cancelled if the person recovers, since it was given only because of the illness. שמואל adds that whenever recovery would cancel the gift, the sick person may also cancel it on purpose, even before recovering. So the mother could take back the gift to רמי and give the property to רב עוקבא instead.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is dangerously ill, on his deathbed
He can take back his gift

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule: if a sick person's gift would be cancelled by recovering, he may also take it back while still sick.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains why a person on his deathbed can keep changing his gifts until he dies.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Shmuel said:
Any case where, if he recovered, he could take it back,
phrases.notes: This means a sick person who gave away everything; if he recovers, the gift is cancelled.

phrases.english: he can take back his gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כֹּל שֶׁאִילּוּ עָמַד – חוֹזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's challenge from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Quoting an earlier authority's rule (שמואל) that supports the ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת thought that since she died without recovering, her first gift could not be cancelled.
steps.terutzMaskana: A sick person whose gift would be cancelled by recovering may also take it back while sick, so the morning gift to רב עוקבא cancels the evening gift.

steps.title: Does שמואל's rule also work for giving to someone else?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת pushes back. Maybe שמואל only allowed a sick person to take back a gift to keep it himself, not to hand it to someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: You could say שמואל meant that he may take it back for himself. Did שמואל say he can take it back in order to give it to someone else?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת challenges how רב נחמן used שמואל's rule. He says the rule may be narrower than רב נחמן thinks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רמי בר חמא's case, the mother took the gift back from רמי in order to give it to רב עוקבא. רב ששת says שמואל's rule might only cover a sick person taking back his gift so he can keep it himself. Giving it to a second person might be a different story.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / you could say (introduces a narrower reading)

phrases.english: Say that שמואל said it — for himself;
phrases.notes: This is רב ששת speaking back to רב נחמן.

phrases.english: for another, did he say it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the source quoted in step 12 really reaches the case in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's use of שמואל's rule to rule for רב עוקבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's rule may cover only taking back a gift to keep it oneself, not moving it to a second person.

steps.title: שמואל said it clearly: for himself or for another
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that שמואל explicitly said the sick person can take back his gift either to keep it or to give it to someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: שמואל said it explicitly — both for himself and for another.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רב ששת's challenge. He does not rely on his own reasoning. He says שמואל spelled it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's narrow reading is rejected. שמואל's rule covers both cases, so the mother could move the gift from רמי to רב עוקבא. That is why רב נחמן ruled for רב עוקבא.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, a שכיב מרע can take back his gift whether he wants to keep the property himself or give it to someone else.

phrases.english: He said to him: שמואל said explicitly:
phrases.notes: Now רב נחמן is answering רב ששת.

phrases.english: both for himself and for another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, בְּפֵירוּשׁ אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to the explicit wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's rule might be limited to keeping the property oneself.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל explicitly included taking it back to give it to another person.

steps.title: רב עמרם חסידא's mother leaves him her notes
steps.stepSummary: A dying mother says her bundle of documents should go to her son עמרם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The mother of רב עמרם the pious had a bundle of documents. When she was dying, she said: Let them be for עמרם my son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story to set up a question about how a dying person's gift takes effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She gives the gift only by speaking. Nothing is handed over and no formal act is done. This sets up the next step's question.

keyTerms.meaning: A bundle of documents (notes of debt)

phrases.english: The mother of רב עמרם the pious
had a bundle of documents.
phrases.notes: These were notes showing that people owed money.

phrases.english: When she was dying, she said:
Let them be for עמרם my son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִימֵּיהּ דְּרַב עַמְרָם חֲסִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new case about the gift of a שכיב מרע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dying mother verbally gives her notes to her son עמרם.

steps.title: The brothers object: he never pulled the bundle
steps.stepSummary: עמרם's brothers argue before רב נחמן that he never acquired the notes because he did no act of acquisition.
steps.simpleTranslation: His brothers came before רב נחמן. They said to him: But he did not pull it!
steps.whatsHappening: The other brothers challenge the gift. They say עמרם never performed a proper act of acquiring the notes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you acquire a movable item by pulling it (משיכה). Notes of debt also usually need a written transfer and to be handed over. Since עמרם did none of this, the brothers claim the notes stay in the inheritance.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulled; משיכה is the act of acquiring movable items

phrases.english: His brothers came before רב נחמן,
they said to him: But he did not pull it!
phrases.notes: Pulling an object toward you is the usual way to make a movable item yours.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: וְהָא לָא מְשַׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the validity of the gift in step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No act of acquisition was done, so ownership should not have passed.

steps.title: A dying person's words count as written and handed over
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the words of a שכיב מרע are treated as if the gift were written and delivered.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The words of a שכיב מרע are considered as written and as handed over.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rejects the brothers' claim and rules that עמרם gets the notes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים gave a dying person's words special power. His speech alone does the job of the writing and the handing over that would normally be needed. So no pulling was required.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is dangerously ill, on his deathbed
As if written and handed over

steps.whatToRemember: דברי שכיב מרע ככתובין וכמסורין דמו: a dying person's spoken gift works with no act of acquisition.

phrases.english: He said to them:
The words of a person on his deathbed
are considered as written and as handed over.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְרֵי שְׁכִיב מְרַע כִּכְתוּבִין וְכִמְסוּרִין דָּמוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the brothers' objection in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special rule for a dying person's gift
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without משיכה, ownership does not pass.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שכיב מרע's words alone transfer the gift.

steps.title: A sister gives to one brother, then switches to another
steps.stepSummary: רב טובי's sister writes her property to him in the morning. In the evening, his crying brother רב אחדבוי convinces her to write it to him instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sister of רב טובי בר רב מתנה wrote her property to רב טובי in the morning. In the evening רב אחדבוי בר רב מתנה came and cried to her. He said: Now people will say that this one is a Torah scholar and that one is not! She wrote it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story of two gifts, one after the other. This sets up רב נחמן's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רמי בר חמא's case, one person gives the same property to two people one after the other. רב אחדבוי was upset that the gift would make him look like the lesser scholar, so the sister rewrote it to him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲחָתֵיהּ דְּרַב טוֹבִי בַּר רַב מַתְנָה
phrases.english: The sister of רב טובי בר רב מתנה
wrote her property

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב טוֹבִי בַּר רַב מַתְנָה – בְּצַפְרָא.
phrases.english: to רב טובי בר רב מתנה — in the morning.

phrases.aramaic: לְפַנְיָא, אֲתָא רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר רַב מַתְנָה
phrases.english: In the evening, רב אחדבוי בר רב מתנה came
and cried to her — he said to her:
Now people will say:
This master is a Torah scholar,
phrases.notes: He means רב טובי, who got the gift.

phrases.english: and that master is not a Torah scholar!
phrases.notes: He means himself, who was left out.

phrases.english: She wrote it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחָתֵיהּ דְּרַב טוֹבִי בַּר רַב מַתְנָה כְּתַבְתִּינְהוּ לְנִכְסַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case with the same pattern as רמי בר חמא's mother in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sister gives her property to one brother and then the same day to another.

steps.title: רב נחמן applies שמואל's rule: the second gift stands
steps.stepSummary: רב טובי comes to רב נחמן, who quotes שמואל: if the giver could take back the gift had he recovered, he can take it back now too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רב נחמן. He said to him: So said שמואל: Any case where, if he recovered, he could take it back — he can take back his gift.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן decides the case using the same rule from שמואל he used before. So the property goes to רב אחדבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the sister's gift was a deathbed gift that would be cancelled if she recovered, she could also change it while still sick. From step 14 we know this works even when she takes it back to give to someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: That if he would recover (stand up from illness)

steps.whyThisMatters: This repeats the case of רמי בר חמא's mother, showing that רב נחמן consistently follows שמואל.

phrases.english: He came before רב נחמן,
phrases.notes: This is רב טובי, who lost the property, coming to complain.

phrases.english: he said to him: So said שמואל:
Any case where, if he recovered, he could take it back,
he can take back his gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כׇּל שֶׁאִילּוּ עָמַד חוֹזֵר, חוֹזֵר בְּמַתְּנָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the case in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sister's second gift, to רב אחדבוי, is valid because a שכיב מרע may take back his gift.

steps.title: רב דימי בר יוסף's sister and her orchard
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. רב דימי בר יוסף's sister owned part of an orchard and gave it to him each time she fell ill.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sister of רב דימי בר יוסף had a piece of an orchard. Every time she became sick, she would transfer it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new case and is setting up what happens next. The story continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She kept giving the orchard to her brother whenever she got sick. This suggests each gift was a deathbed gift that fell away when she recovered. The question of what happens in the end comes in the continuation.

phrases.english: The sister of רב דימי בר יוסף
had a piece of an orchard,
every time she was sick
she would transfer it to him,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחָתֵיהּ דְּרַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף הֲוָה לַהּ פִּיסְקְתָא דְפַרְדֵּיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens another case about deathbed gifts. It is continued in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: a sister repeatedly gives her orchard to her brother whenever she is sick.
